## QAIC helper for quasi-likelihood candidate models

```{r qaic_helper, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
qaic_deviance <- function(fit) {
  d <- tryCatch(stats::deviance(fit), error=function(e) NA_real_)
  phi <- tryCatch(summary(fit)$dispersion, error=function(e) NA_real_)
  k <- length(stats::coef(fit))
  if (!is.finite(d) || !is.finite(phi) || phi <= 0 || !is.finite(k))
    return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(d/phi + 2*k)
}
```

When likelihood-based QAIC is unavailable for a quasi-likelihood fit, this
explicit deviance-based quantity is used only for comparing models fitted to
the same outcome/data structure. It is not silently treated as ordinary AIC.


# 1. Analysis plan

This document executes the four protocol objectives sequentially:

1. **Exposure–response:** estimate the UTCI–all-cause mortality exposure–response relationship using a time-stratified case-crossover design and DLNM.
2. **Lag effects:** characterize lag-specific and cumulative effects through 0–21 days and evaluate possible mortality displacement/harvesting.
3. **Temporal shifts:** compare prespecified periods only after verifying the observed data coverage, using a common locked DLNM specification and a formal coefficient-contrast test.
4. **Vulnerable groups:** evaluate effect modification by age and sex and, if a valid residency variable is present, residency status.

The protocol specifies individual-level mortality data, UTCI exposure, a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional regression, DLNM exposure and lag splines, and a 0–21-day lag objective. The protocol also proposes comparison of 1990–2004 versus 2005–2018, but the actual years present in `analysis_ready_matrix` are treated as authoritative rather than assuming those periods exist. 

**Important computational decision:** the old approach of fitting and retaining every candidate model, plus a 1,000-fold data-resample/refit bootstrap, is deliberately not used. Candidate fits are run **one at a time**, only diagnostics are retained, and the selected model is then refitted once. For derived quantities such as MMT, the primary uncertainty calculation uses **parametric Monte Carlo simulation from the fitted coefficient covariance matrix**, not repeated model refitting. This preserves coefficient-sampling uncertainty while avoiding hundreds/thousands of large case-crossover model fits.

# 4. Helper functions

## 4.1 Model fitting

```{r helpers-models}
build_lag_basis <- function(max_lag, lag_df = NULL, lag_knots = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(lag_knots)) {
    list(fun = "ns", knots = lag_knots, intercept = TRUE)
  } else {
    list(fun = "ns", df = lag_df, intercept = TRUE)
  }
}

compute_qaic <- function(fit) {
  ll <- tryCatch(as.numeric(logLik(fit)), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  phi <- tryCatch(summary(fit)$dispersion, error = function(e) NA_real_)
  k <- length(coef(fit))
  if (is.na(ll) || is.na(phi)) return(NA_real_)
  -2 * ll / phi + 2 * k
}

compute_model_metrics <- function(
    fit, cb, MMT, max_lag, exposure_df, lag_df, max_RR = NA_real_) {

  rank_cb <- qr(cb)$rank

  tibble(
    max_lag = max_lag,
    exposure_df = exposure_df,
    lag_df = lag_df,
    converged = isTRUE(fit$converged),
    dispersion = tryCatch(summary(fit)$dispersion, error = function(e) NA_real_),
    QAIC = compute_qaic(fit),
    rank = rank_cb,
    n_basis = ncol(cb),
    full_rank = rank_cb == ncol(cb),
    kappa = tryCatch(kappa(cb), error = function(e) NA_real_),
    MMT = MMT,
    max_RR = max_RR
  )
}

run_dlnm_spec <- function(
    data, max_lag, exposure_df, lag_df,
    var_knots = NULL, lag_knots = NULL,
    exposure_var = EXPOSURE_VAR, outcome_var = OUTCOME_VAR,
    stratum_var = STRATUM_VAR, lag_prefix = LAG_PREFIX,
    mmt_probs = c(params$mmt_search_low, params$mmt_search_high),
    by = 0.1, cen = NULL) {

  lag_cols <- paste0(lag_prefix, 0:max_lag)

  if (!all(lag_cols %in% names(data))) return(NULL)

  lag_matrix <- as.matrix(data[, lag_cols, drop = FALSE])
  keep <- complete.cases(lag_matrix) &
    !is.na(data[[exposure_var]]) &
    !is.na(data[[outcome_var]]) &
    !is.na(data[[stratum_var]])

  d <- data[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  lag_matrix <- lag_matrix[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)

  if (is.null(var_knots)) {
    var_knots <- dlnm::equalknots(
      d[[exposure_var]], fun = "ns", df = exposure_df
    )
  }

  lag_basis <- build_lag_basis(max_lag, lag_df, lag_knots)

  cb <- tryCatch(
    dlnm::crossbasis(
      lag_matrix,
      lag = max_lag,
      argvar = list(fun = "ns", knots = var_knots),
      arglag = lag_basis
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(cb)) return(NULL)

  fit <- tryCatch(
    gnm::gnm(
      as.formula(paste0(outcome_var, " ~ cb")),
      eliminate = factor(d[[stratum_var]]),
      family = quasipoisson(),
      data = d
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  q <- quantile(
    d[[exposure_var]],
    probs = mmt_probs,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )

  pred0 <- tryCatch(
    dlnm::crosspred(cb, fit, by = by, model.link = "log"),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  MMT <- NA_real_
  max_RR <- NA_real_

  if (!is.null(pred0)) {
    in_search <- pred0$predvar >= q[1] &
      pred0$predvar <= q[2]

    if (any(in_search)) {
      MMT <- pred0$predvar[in_search][
        which.min(pred0$allRRfit[in_search])
      ]
    }

    max_RR <- max(pred0$allRRfit, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  centre_value <- if (is.null(cen)) {
    if (is.na(MMT)) median(d[[exposure_var]], na.rm = TRUE) else MMT
  } else {
    cen
  }

  pred <- tryCatch(
    dlnm::crosspred(
      cb, fit, cen = centre_value, by = by, model.link = "log"
    ),
    error = function(e) pred0
  )

  list(
    cb = cb,
    fit = fit,
    pred = pred,
    pred0 = pred0,
    MMT = MMT,
    var_knots = var_knots,
    lag_basis = lag_basis,
    metrics = compute_model_metrics(
      fit, cb, MMT, max_lag, exposure_df, lag_df, max_RR
    )
  )
}
```

## 4.2 Model-selection gates

```{r helpers-selection}
apply_decision_rule <- function(
    metrics_tbl,
    mmt_range = c(params$mmt_search_low, params$mmt_search_high),
    kappa_max = params$kappa_max,
    dispersion_max = params$dispersion_max,
    qaic_tol = params$qaic_tolerance,
    max_rr_threshold = params$max_rr_plausible,
    min_mmt_threshold = params$mmt_min_plausible) {

  gate_report <- metrics_tbl %>%
    mutate(
      fail_convergence = !converged | !full_rank,
      fail_kappa = !is.na(kappa) & kappa > kappa_max,
      fail_dispersion = !is.na(dispersion) & dispersion > dispersion_max,
      fail_mmt_range = is.na(MMT) |
        MMT < quantile(dat[[EXPOSURE_VAR]], mmt_range[1], na.rm = TRUE) |
        MMT > quantile(dat[[EXPOSURE_VAR]], mmt_range[2], na.rm = TRUE),
      fail_max_rr = !is.na(max_RR) & max_RR > max_rr_threshold,
      fail_min_mmt = !is.na(MMT) & MMT < min_mmt_threshold
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      passed_all_gates =
        !fail_convergence &
        !fail_kappa &
        !fail_dispersion &
        !fail_mmt_range &
        !fail_max_rr &
        !fail_min_mmt
    )

  candidates <- gate_report %>%
    filter(passed_all_gates)

  if (!nrow(candidates)) {
    return(list(
      best_model = NULL,
      candidates = candidates,
      gate_report = gate_report
    ))
  }

  # Prefer the best likelihood-supported model, then QAIC within tolerance,
  # then parsimony and numerical stability.
  best_ll <- max(candidates$QAIC * -1, na.rm = TRUE)
  candidates <- candidates %>%
    mutate(ll_rank = QAIC * -1) %>%
    filter(ll_rank >= best_ll - qaic_tol) %>%
    arrange(QAIC, exposure_df, lag_df, n_basis, kappa)

  list(
    best_model = candidates[1, , drop = FALSE],
    candidates = candidates,
    gate_report = gate_report
  )
}
```

## 5.2 Candidate crossbasis search — memory-safe implementation

**Memory rule:** do not create `all_results` containing every fitted model. Each candidate is fitted, reduced to diagnostics, and immediately released.

```{r obj1-candidate-search}
candidate_specs <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  max_lag = params$candidate_lags,
  exposure_df = params$exposure_df_candidates,
  lag_df = params$lag_df_candidates
) %>%
  mutate(
    model_id = paste0(
      "Lag", max_lag, "_E", exposure_df, "_L", lag_df
    )
  )

candidate_metrics <- vector("list", nrow(candidate_specs))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidate_specs))) {

  spec <- candidate_specs[i, ]

  message(
    "Fitting ", spec$model_id, " (", i, "/", nrow(candidate_specs), ")"
  )

  res <- tryCatch(
    run_dlnm_spec(
      dat,
      max_lag = spec$max_lag,
      exposure_df = spec$exposure_df,
      lag_df = spec$lag_df
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (!is.null(res)) {
    candidate_metrics[[i]] <- res$metrics %>%
      mutate(model_id = spec$model_id)
  }

  # Explicitly release the large crossbasis/model before the next candidate.
  rm(res)
  invisible(gc())
}

diagnostics_tbl <- bind_rows(candidate_metrics)

write.csv(
  diagnostics_tbl,
  "Results/Crossbasis/Candidate_Model_Diagnostics.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

diagnostics_tbl %>%
  arrange(QAIC) %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>%
  flextable::autofit()
```

## 5.3 Lock the primary specification

```{r obj1-model-selection}
decision <- apply_decision_rule(diagnostics_tbl)

decision$gate_report %>%
  arrange(desc(passed_all_gates), QAIC) %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>%
  flextable::autofit()
```

```{r obj1-lock}
if (is.null(decision$best_model)) {
  stop(
    "No candidate passed all diagnostic/plausibility gates. ",
    "Do not relax the gates automatically. Inspect ",
    "Results/Crossbasis/Candidate_Model_Diagnostics.csv and the gate report."
  )
}

best_id <- decision$best_model$model_id[[1]]

best_row <- candidate_specs %>%
  filter(model_id == best_id)

best_spec <- list(
  model_id = best_id,
  max_lag = best_spec$max_lag[[1]],
  exposure_df = best_row$exposure_df[[1]],
  lag_df = best_row$lag_df[[1]]
)

# Refit the selected model ONCE.
best_fit <- run_dlnm_spec(
  dat,
  max_lag = best_spec$max_lag,
  exposure_df = best_spec$exposure_df,
  lag_df = best_spec$lag_df
)

if (is.null(best_fit)) {
  stop("Selected model could not be refitted.")
}

best_spec$var_knots <- best_fit$var_knots
best_spec$lag_knots <- best_fit$lag_basis$knots
best_spec$MMT <- best_fit$MMT
best_spec$cen <- best_fit$MMT

MMT <- best_fit$MMT
cb <- best_fit$cb
fit <- best_fit$fit
final_pred <- best_fit$pred

saveRDS(best_spec, "Results/Objects/best_specification.rds")
saveRDS(best_fit, "Results/Objects/best_model.rds")

write.csv(
  as.data.frame(best_fit$metrics),
  "Results/Crossbasis/Locked_Model_Diagnostics.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 5.5 Primary contrasts

The contrasts are evaluated at percentiles because they are interpretable and avoid extrapolation beyond the observed exposure distribution.

```{r obj1-contrasts}
case_p <- quantile(
  dat[[EXPOSURE_VAR]],
  probs = c(.01, .05, .50, .95, .99),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

contrast_values <- c(
  "P01_vs_MMT" = case_p[1],
  "P05_vs_MMT" = case_p[2],
  "P95_vs_MMT" = case_p[4],
  "P99_vs_MMT" = case_p[5],
  "MMT_plus_5" = MMT + 5,
  "MMT_plus_8" = MMT + 8
)

get_rr <- function(pred, at) {
  idx <- which.min(abs(pred$predvar - at))
  tibble(
    exposure = names(at),
    UTCI = pred$predvar[idx],
    RR = pred$allRRfit[idx],
    lower = pred$allRRlow[idx],
    upper = pred$allRRhigh[idx]
  )
}

obj1_contrasts <- purrr::map_dfr(
  contrast_values,
  ~ get_rr(final_pred, c(value = .x))
)

# Replace the temporary exposure labels with stable names.
obj1_contrasts$exposure <- names(contrast_values)

obj1_contrasts %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>% flextable::autofit()

write.csv(
  obj1_contrasts,
  "Results/Crossbasis/Table_Objective1_RR_Contrasts.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 6. Objective 1 — centre-specific models and multivariate meta-analysis

Only the reduced coefficient vectors and covariance matrices are retained for each centre. Full centre model objects are not accumulated in memory.

```{r centre-functions}
fit_one_centre_reduced <- function(
    centre_data, centre_id, spec, cen,
    min_deaths = params$min_centre_deaths,
    max_kappa = params$kappa_max) {

  n_deaths <- sum(centre_data[[OUTCOME_VAR]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (n_deaths < min_deaths) {
    return(tibble(
      centreid = centre_id,
      included = FALSE,
      reason = paste0(
        "Too few deaths: ", n_deaths,
        " < ", min_deaths
      )
    ))
  }

  res <- run_dlnm_spec(
    centre_data,
    max_lag = spec$max_lag,
    exposure_df = spec$exposure_df,
    lag_df = spec$lag_df,
    var_knots = spec$var_knots,
    lag_knots = spec$lag_knots,
    cen = cen
  )

  if (is.null(res)) {
    return(tibble(
      centreid = centre_id,
      included = FALSE,
      reason = "Model fitting failed"
    ))
  }

  m <- res$metrics

  if (!isTRUE(m$converged)) {
    return(tibble(
      centreid = centre_id,
      included = FALSE,
      reason = "Non-convergence"
    ))
  }

  if (!isTRUE(m$full_rank)) {
    return(tibble(
      centreid = centre_id,
      included = FALSE,
      reason = "Rank-deficient crossbasis"
    ))
  }

  if (!is.na(m$kappa) && m$kappa > max_kappa) {
    return(tibble(
      centreid = centre_id,
      included = FALSE,
      reason = paste0("Kappa > ", max_kappa)
    ))
  }

  reduced <- tryCatch(
    dlnm::crossreduce(res$cb, res$fit, cen = cen),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(reduced)) {
    return(tibble(
      centreid = centre_id,
      included = FALSE,
      reason = "crossreduce() failed"
    ))
  }

  tibble(
    centreid = centre_id,
    included = TRUE,
    reason = NA_character_,
    centre_name = as.character(dplyr::first(centre_data$centre_name)),
    country = as.character(dplyr::first(centre_data$country)),
    climate_zone = as.character(dplyr::first(centre_data$climate_zone)),
    n_deaths = n_deaths,
    coefficients = list(unname(reduced$coefficients)),
    vcov = list(reduced$vcov),
    metrics = list(m)
  )
}

fit_all_centres_reduced <- function(data, spec, cen) {

  groups <- split(data, data$centreid)

  out <- vector("list", length(groups))
  ids <- names(groups)

  for (i in seq_along(groups)) {
    message("Centre ", i, "/", length(groups), ": ", ids[i])

    out[[i]] <- fit_one_centre_reduced(
      groups[[i]], ids[i], spec, cen
    )

    # Remove group-level objects before the next centre.
    rm(groups[[i]])
    invisible(gc())
  }

  bind_rows(out)
}
```

# 7. Bootstrap / Monte Carlo uncertainty — computationally safe version

## 7.1 Why a conventional bootstrap is not the primary method

A naive bootstrap would repeatedly resample the case-crossover data and refit the DLNM. With 186,628 rows, 21+ lag columns, conditional strata, and nonlinear crossbasis terms, hundreds or thousands of full refits can cause:

- very high RAM use;
- duplicated large design matrices;
- long runtimes;
- parallel-worker memory multiplication;
- failed convergence in some resamples;
- excessive temporary model objects.

For this analysis, the primary uncertainty for **derived quantities from the locked model** is therefore obtained by drawing from the fitted multivariate normal coefficient distribution and evaluating the nonlinear prediction repeatedly. This is computationally much cheaper because it does not recreate the data or refit `gnm`.

The existing project script already moved away from a 1,000-refit bootstrap to this Monte Carlo approach. That decision is retained and strengthened here by storing only compact matrices and using chunked simulation.

## 7.2 Memory-safe Monte Carlo MMT uncertainty

```{r mmt-mc}
mmt_mc_uncertainty <- function(
    fit, cb, exposure_data,
    mmt_range = c(params$mmt_search_low, params$mmt_search_high),
    by = 0.1, nsim = params$mc_draws,
    seed = params$seed,
    chunk_size = 250) {

  set.seed(seed)

  b <- coef(fit)
  V <- vcov(fit)

  # Numerical stabilisation for tiny asymmetries in the covariance matrix.
  V <- (V + t(V)) / 2

  # Cholesky is substantially more memory-efficient than storing all
  # coefficient draws at once.
  R <- tryCatch(chol(V), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(R)) {
    V <- V + diag(1e-8, nrow(V))
    R <- chol(V)
  }

  q <- quantile(
    exposure_data,
    probs = mmt_range,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )

  base_pred <- dlnm::crosspred(
    cb, coef = b, vcov = V,
    model.link = "log", by = by
  )

  predvar <- base_pred$predvar
  in_range <- predvar >= q[1] & predvar <= q[2]

  mmt_sim <- rep(NA_real_, nsim)

  # Do not allocate nsim x n_prediction_points matrices.
  # One chunk is evaluated and immediately discarded.
  starts <- seq(1, nsim, by = chunk_size)

  for (s in starts) {

    e <- min(s + chunk_size - 1, nsim)
    n <- e - s + 1

    Z <- matrix(rnorm(n * length(b)), nrow = n)
    beta_draws <- sweep(Z %*% R, 2, b, "+")

    for (j in seq_len(n)) {

      # crosspred() requires the coefficient vector corresponding to the
      # crossbasis. We do not request a covariance matrix for each draw.
      pr <- tryCatch(
        dlnm::crosspred(
          cb,
          coef = beta_draws[j, ],
          model.link = "log",
          by = by
        ),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )

      if (is.null(pr)) next

      log_rr <- log(pr$allRRfit)

      if (any(in_range)) {
        x <- predvar[in_range]
        y <- log_rr[in_range]

        if (length(unique(x)) >= 4 && all(is.finite(y))) {
          sf <- tryCatch(
            splinefun(x, y, method = "natural"),
            error = function(e) NULL
          )

          if (!is.null(sf)) {
            opt <- tryCatch(
              optimize(
                sf,
                interval = range(x)
              ),
              error = function(e) NULL
            )

            if (!is.null(opt)) {
              mmt_sim[s + j - 1] <- opt$minimum
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }

    rm(Z, beta_draws)
    invisible(gc())
  }

  list(
    mmt = mmt_sim,
    predvar = predvar,
    fitted = base_pred$allRRfit
  )
}

mmt_mc <- mmt_mc_uncertainty(
  fit,
  cb,
  dat[[EXPOSURE_VAR]]
)

mmt_summary <- tibble(
  simulations = sum(is.finite(mmt_mc$mmt)),
  failed = sum(!is.finite(mmt_mc$mmt)),
  median_MMT = median(mmt_mc$mmt, na.rm = TRUE),
  CI_low = quantile(mmt_mc$mmt, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
  CI_high = quantile(mmt_mc$mmt, .975, na.rm = TRUE)
)

mmt_summary %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>% flextable::autofit()

write.csv(
  mmt_summary,
  "Results/Diagnostics/MMT_MonteCarlo_Uncertainty.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  mmt_mc$mmt,
  "Results/Diagnostics/MMT_MonteCarlo_Draws.rds"
)
```

## 7.3 Optional genuine resampling bootstrap

This is **not run by default**. It is included only as a sensitivity analysis if reviewers specifically require nonparametric resampling.

The bootstrap is performed at the **case/stratum level**, not by independently resampling individual rows, because rows within a case-crossover stratum are dependent. It is also deliberately capped and sequential.

```{r optional-bootstrap, eval=FALSE}
# OPTIONAL ONLY.
# Do not run thousands of full refits on the complete matrix.
#
# Recommended reviewer-sensitivity configuration:
#   B = 100–200
#   sequential execution
#   no parallel workers
#   save only scalar/compact results after each iteration
#
# A full nonparametric bootstrap remains computationally expensive and can
# still fail in individual replicates. It should not replace the primary
# coefficient-Monte-Carlo uncertainty analysis above.

bootstrap_mmt_refit <- function(
    data, spec, B = 200, seed = params$seed) {

  set.seed(seed)

  strata <- unique(data[[STRATUM_VAR]])
  out <- rep(NA_real_, B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {

    sampled_strata <- sample(strata, length(strata), replace = TRUE)

    boot <- purrr::map_dfr(
      sampled_strata,
      function(s) {
        data[data[[STRATUM_VAR]] == s, , drop = FALSE]
      }
    )

    res <- tryCatch(
      run_dlnm_spec(
        boot,
        max_lag = spec$max_lag,
        exposure_df = spec$exposure_df,
        lag_df = spec$lag_df,
        var_knots = spec$var_knots,
        lag_knots = spec$lag_knots
      ),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )

    if (!is.null(res)) out[b] <- res$MMT

    rm(boot, res)
    invisible(gc())

    # Incremental checkpoint prevents losing completed iterations.
    saveRDS(
      out,
      file.path(
        "Results/Diagnostics",
        paste0("Optional_bootstrap_MMT_B", B, ".rds")
      )
    )
  }

  out
}

# Example:
# boot_mmt <- bootstrap_mmt_refit(dat, best_spec, B = 200)
```

# 8. Objective 2 — lag-response and harvesting

```{r obj2-lag-helper}
summarize_lag_windows <- function(pred, at, max_lag, label) {

  idx <- which.min(abs(pred$predvar - at))
  log_rr_by_lag <- log(pred$matRRfit[idx, ])
  lag_days <- 0:(length(log_rr_by_lag) - 1)

  windows <- list(
    Immediate = c(0, 0),
    Short = c(1, 3),
    Medium = c(4, 7),
    Delayed = c(8, min(14, max_lag)),
    Harvesting = c(min(15, max_lag), max_lag)
  )

  windows <- windows[
    !duplicated(purrr::map(windows, ~ paste(.x, collapse = "-")))
  ]

  purrr::map_dfr(names(windows), function(w) {

    rng <- windows[[w]]
    sel <- lag_days >= rng[1] & lag_days <= rng[2]

    tibble(
      exposure_condition = label,
      exposure_UTCI = pred$predvar[idx],
      window = w,
      lag_days = paste0(rng[1], "-", rng[2]),
      RR = exp(sum(log_rr_by_lag[sel], na.rm = TRUE))
    )
  })
}
```

## 8.1 Lag-response slices

```{r obj2-lag-curves, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
par(mfrow = c(3, 1))

for (nm in names(lag_conditions)) {

  at <- lag_conditions[[nm]]
  at_snapped <- final_pred$predvar[
    which.min(abs(final_pred$predvar - at))
  ]

  plot(
    final_pred,
    "slices",
    var = at_snapped,
    ci = "lines",
    xlab = "Lag (days)",
    ylab = "RR",
    main = paste0(
      nm, ": UTCI = ", round(at_snapped, 1), "°C"
    )
  )

  abline(h = 1, lty = 2)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

**Interpretation rule:** a decline below RR=1 at later lags is not automatically evidence of harvesting. The displacement interpretation is strongest when an early excess is followed by a compensatory deficit, while the cumulative association is simultaneously examined. A cumulative RR that remains elevated through the later lag period is more consistent with persistent excess mortality than simple short-term displacement.

# 9. Objective 3 — temporal shifts

The protocol gives 1990–2004 versus 2005–2018 as an example. The actual matrix is checked first. The periods are **not silently replaced by the old example 2009–2012 versus 2013–2016**.

```{r obj3-periods}
data_years <- range(dat$year, na.rm = TRUE)

protocol_periods <- list(
  early = c(1990, 2004),
  late = c(2005, 2018)
)

periods <- lapply(
  protocol_periods,
  function(x) c(
    max(x[1], data_years[1]),
    min(x[2], data_years[2])
  )
)

valid_periods <- periods[
  vapply(
    periods,
    function(x) x[1] <= x[2],
    logical(1)
  )
]

period_check <- tibble(
  period = names(periods),
  requested_start = sapply(protocol_periods, `[`, 1),
  requested_end = sapply(protocol_periods, `[`, 2),
  observed_start = sapply(periods, `[`, 1),
  observed_end = sapply(periods, `[`, 2),
  valid = names(periods) %in% names(valid_periods)
)

period_check %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>% flextable::autofit()

write.csv(
  period_check,
  "Results/TemporalAdaptation/Period_Check.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r obj3-period-models}
fit_period <- function(data, rng, spec, cen) {

  pd <- data %>%
    filter(
      year >= rng[1],
      year <= rng[2]
    )

  if (!nrow(pd)) return(NULL)

  centre_res <- fit_all_centres_reduced(
    pd, spec, cen
  )

  inc <- centre_res %>% filter(included)

  if (nrow(inc) < 2) return(NULL)

  cm <- do.call(rbind, inc$coefficients)

  mf <- tryCatch(
    mixmeta::mixmeta(
      cm,
      inc$vcov,
      method = "reml"
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(mf)) return(NULL)

  list(
    range = rng,
    centre_results = centre_res,
    meta_fit = mf,
    n_centres = nrow(inc),
    deaths = sum(inc$n_deaths)
  )
}

period_fits <- purrr::imap(
  valid_periods,
  ~ fit_period(dat, .x, best_spec, MMT)
)

period_fits <- period_fits[!vapply(period_fits, is.null, logical(1))]

if (length(period_fits) < 2) {
  warning(
    "Fewer than two valid temporal periods were available; ",
    "formal temporal contrast cannot be estimated."
  )
}
```

## 9.1 Formal comparison

```{r obj3-formal-contrast}
if (length(period_fits) >= 2) {

  period_names <- names(period_fits)[1:2]

  b1 <- coef(period_fits[[1]]$meta_fit)
  b2 <- coef(period_fits[[2]]$meta_fit)

  V1 <- vcov(period_fits[[1]]$meta_fit)
  V2 <- vcov(period_fits[[2]]$meta_fit)

  delta <- b2 - b1
  Vdelta <- (V1 + V2) / 1

  W <- as.numeric(
    t(delta) %*% solve(Vdelta, delta)
  )

  df_wald <- length(delta)
  p_wald <- pchisq(W, df = df_wald, lower.tail = FALSE)

  temporal_wald <- tibble(
    comparison = paste0(
      period_names[2], " minus ", period_names[1]
    ),
    Wald_statistic = W,
    df = df_wald,
    p_value = p_wald
  )

  temporal_wald %>%
    flextable::flextable() %>% flextable::autofit()

  write.csv(
    temporal_wald,
    "Results/TemporalAdaptation/Formal_Temporal_Contrast.csv",
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

## 9.2 Period-specific pooled curves

```{r obj3-curves, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
if (length(period_fits) >= 2) {

  pred_periods <- purrr::imap(
    period_fits,
    ~ dlnm::crosspred(
      cb,
      coef = coef(.x$meta_fit),
      vcov = vcov(.x$meta_fit),
      model.link = "log",
      by = 0.1,
      cen = MMT
    )
  )

  plot(
    pred_periods[[1]], "overall",
    xlab = "UTCI (°C)",
    ylab = "Relative Risk",
    main = "Temporal comparison of UTCI–mortality curves"
  )

  lines(
    pred_periods[[2]]$predvar,
    pred_periods[[2]]$allRRfit,
    lwd = 2
  )

  abline(h = 1, lty = 2)
  abline(v = MMT, lty = 2)
}
```

Temporal differences are interpreted as **changes in vulnerability over time**, not automatically as proof of causal adaptation. Changes in centre composition, mortality ascertainment, exposure distributions, population structure, and other unmeasured factors can also produce temporal differences.

# 10. Objective 4 — vulnerable groups

## 10.1 Validate sex coding before interpretation

```{r obj4-sex-qc}
sex_distribution <- dat %>%
  count(sex, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(percent = 100 * n / sum(n))
```

The matrix contains numeric sex codes, but the supplied matrix does not include a codebook in the columns shown. Therefore the analysis does **not** silently label code 1 as male or code 2 as female. The statistical results are first produced using the observed codes; publication labels must be attached only after the project data dictionary confirms their meaning.

## 10.2 Age groups based on the protocol thresholds

The protocol identifies children around age 5 and elderly people around age 65. Because `age_at_death` is available, the primary subgroup definitions are generated directly from the continuous age variable rather than assuming that the existing factor labels correspond exactly to those thresholds.

```{r obj4-age-groups}

    subgroup_age_elderly = age_at_death >= 65

    sum(dat$subgroup_age_elderly & dat[[OUTCOME_VAR]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)

  rows = c(

    sum(dat$subgroup_age_elderly, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## 10.5 Formal effect-modification tests

Because the age-defined groups and sex-code groups are mutually exclusive, their coefficient estimates can be compared using a multivariate Wald test, provided both subgroup models converge and use the same locked basis.

```{r obj4-interactions}
wald_compare <- function(res1, res2, label1, label2) {

  if (is.null(res1) || is.null(res2)) return(NULL)

  r1 <- tryCatch(
    dlnm::crossreduce(res1$cb, res1$fit, cen = MMT),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  r2 <- tryCatch(
    dlnm::crossreduce(res2$cb, res2$fit, cen = MMT),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(r1) || is.null(r2)) return(NULL)

  if (length(r1$coefficients) != length(r2$coefficients)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  delta <- r2$coefficients - r1$coefficients
  Vdelta <- r1$vcov + r2$vcov

  W <- as.numeric(
    t(delta) %*% solve(Vdelta, delta)
  )

  tibble(
    group_1 = label1,
    group_2 = label2,
    Wald = W,
    df = length(delta),
    p_value = pchisq(
      W, df = length(delta), lower.tail = FALSE
    )
  )
}

interaction_results <- bind_rows(
  wald_compare(
    subgroup_fits$Age_le_5,
    subgroup_fits$Age_ge_65,
    "Age <=5",
    "Age >=65"
  )
)

for (sx in sort(unique(na.omit(dat$sex)))) {
  other_sx <- sort(unique(na.omit(dat$sex)))
  other_sx <- other_sx[other_sx != sx][1]

  if (!is.na(other_sx)) {
    nm1 <- paste0("Sex_code_", sx)
    nm2 <- paste0("Sex_code_", other_sx)

    interaction_results <- bind_rows(
      interaction_results,
      wald_compare(
        subgroup_fits[[nm1]],
        subgroup_fits[[nm2]],
        nm1,
        nm2
      )
    )
  }
}

interaction_results %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>% flextable::autofit()

write.csv(
  interaction_results,
  "Results/Subgroups/Formal_Effect_Modification_Tests.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 11. Optional attributable mortality analysis

Attributable fraction is a downstream analysis in the supplied project materials and is not relabelled as protocol Objective 1. It should only be run when the installed `FluMoDL` package and its `attrdl()` implementation are available and compatible with the fitted model.

```{r attributable-fraction}
if (requireNamespace("FluMoDL", quietly = TRUE) &&
    "attrdl" %in% getNamespaceExports("FluMoDL")) {

  af_heat <- tryCatch(
    FluMoDL::attrdl(
      x = dat[[EXPOSURE_VAR]],
      basis = cb,
      cases = dat[[OUTCOME_VAR]],
      model = fit,
      cen = MMT,
      range = c(MMT, Inf),
      type = "af"
    ),
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )

  af_cold <- tryCatch(
    FluMoDL::attrdl(
      x = dat[[EXPOSURE_VAR]],
      basis = cb,
      cases = dat[[OUTCOME_VAR]],
      model = fit,
      cen = MMT,
      range = c(-Inf, MMT),
      type = "af"
    ),
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )

  af_table <- tibble(
    component = c("Cold below MMT", "Heat at/above MMT"),
    attributable_fraction = c(af_cold, af_heat)
  )

} else {

  af_table <- tibble(
    component = c("Cold below MMT", "Heat at/above MMT"),
    attributable_fraction = NA_real_,
    status = "Not run: compatible FluMoDL::attrdl() unavailable"
  )
}

af_table %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>% flextable::autofit()

write.csv(
  af_table,

)
```

# 17. Interpretation guardrails

- Report the primary DLNM specification actually selected by the data and diagnostic gates.
- Do not describe an RR below 1 at a later lag as harvesting without examining the full lag pattern and cumulative association.
- Do not infer causal adaptation solely from early/late period differences.
- Do not label numeric sex codes until the data dictionary confirms their meaning.
- Do not report a residency effect because the displayed matrix does not contain a residency-status variable.
- Do not use the old 2009–2012 versus 2013–2016 example periods unless the actual dataset and protocol are explicitly revised to those years.
- Do not use a 1,000+ full-data bootstrap as the default uncertainty engine.
- Do not run large-scale parallel model fitting by default: worker processes can duplicate the 186,628-row matrix and substantially increase peak RAM.
- If a genuine nonparametric bootstrap is required by peer review, use a small sequential sensitivity bootstrap, checkpoint every replicate, and store only compact outputs.



# Lag 7 versus Lag 14 versus Lag 21: empirical lag-selection comparison

This section must be completed before a primary maximum lag is manually locked.
It compares the three E3_L3 specifications using:

1. cumulative exposure-response curves with 95% confidence intervals;
2. minimum-mortality temperature (MMT);
3. maximum and mean differences between cumulative curves;
4. lag-specific exposure-response surfaces;
5. explicit examination of lags 15–21 in the Lag21 model;
6. a compact decision table.

No lag is automatically declared primary.

```{r lag_selection_comparison, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dlnm)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

get_existing <- function(...) {
  nm <- c(...)
  hit <- nm[vapply(nm, exists, logical(1), inherits = TRUE)]
  if (!length(hit)) {
    stop(
      "Could not find any of the expected objects: ",
      paste(nm, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
  get(hit[[1]], inherits = TRUE)
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Retrieve the three fitted models and their corresponding crossbasis
# objects. Change ONLY these aliases if the fitting section uses different
# object names.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

fit7 <- get_existing(
  "fit_lag7_e3_l3", "fit_Lag7_E3_L3", "fit7_e3_l3"
)

fit14 <- get_existing(
  "fit_lag14_e3_l3", "fit_Lag14_E3_L3", "fit14_e3_l3"
)

fit21 <- get_existing(
  "fit_lag21_e3_l3", "fit_Lag21_E3_L3", "fit21_e3_l3"
)

cb7 <- get_existing(
  "cb_lag7_e3_l3", "cb_Lag7_E3_L3", "cb7_e3_l3"
)

cb14 <- get_existing(
  "cb_lag14_e3_l3", "cb_Lag14_E3_L3", "cb14_e3_l3"
)

cb21 <- get_existing(
  "cb_lag21_e3_l3", "cb_Lag21_E3_L3", "cb21_e3_l3"
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exposure used by the candidate models.
# The script does not invent an exposure variable.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

utci_var <- intersect(
  c("utci_mean", "utci_min", "utci_max"),
  names(analysis_ready_matrix)
)[1]

if (is.na(utci_var)) {
  stop(
    "No UTCI exposure variable found. Expected one of: ",
    paste(c("utci_mean", "utci_min", "utci_max"), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

x_obs <- analysis_ready_matrix[[utci_var]]
x_obs <- x_obs[is.finite(x_obs)]

if (!length(x_obs)) {
  stop("No finite UTCI observations are available.")
}

# Common grid = essential for direct comparison.
x_seq <- seq(
  quantile(x_obs, 0.005, na.rm = TRUE),
  quantile(x_obs, 0.995, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 250
)

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CUMULATIVE RR
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_cumulative_rr <- function(fit, cb, lag_label, x_seq) {

  cp <- dlnm::crosspred(
    cb,
    model = fit,
    at = x_seq,
    cen = NA,
    cumul = TRUE
  )

  rr <- data.frame(
    utci = x_seq,
    rr = as.numeric(cp$cumRRfit),
    lower = as.numeric(cp$cumRRlow),
    upper = as.numeric(cp$cumRRhigh),
    lag = lag_label
  )

  rr$mmt <- rr$utci[which.min(rr$rr)]

  rr
}

rr7 <- make_cumulative_rr(fit7, cb7, "Lag 7 days", x_seq)
rr14 <- make_cumulative_rr(fit14, cb14, "Lag 14 days", x_seq)
rr21 <- make_cumulative_rr(fit21, cb21, "Lag 21 days", x_seq)

rr_all <- bind_rows(rr7, rr14, rr21)

write.csv(
  rr_all,
  "outputs/Cumulative_RR_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CUMULATIVE RR PLOT
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_cumulative_lags <- ggplot(
  rr_all,
  aes(x = utci, y = rr, linetype = lag)
) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = lag),
    alpha = 0.10,
    colour = NA
  ) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +

  labs(
    title =
      "Cumulative UTCI–mortality association across alternative lag windows",
    subtitle =
      "E3_L3 specifications; common UTCI range",
    x = "UTCI (°C)",
    y = "Cumulative relative risk",
    linetype = "Maximum lag",
    fill = "Maximum lag"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(p_cumulative_lags)

ggsave(
  "outputs/Figure_Cumulative_RR_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.png",
  p_cumulative_lags,
  width = 9,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 600
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NUMERICAL COMPARISON OF CURVES
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

rr_wide <- rr_all %>%
  select(utci, lag, rr) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = lag,
    values_from = rr
  )

n7 <- names(rr_wide)[grepl("^Lag 7", names(rr_wide))]
n14 <- names(rr_wide)[grepl("^Lag 14", names(rr_wide))]
n21 <- names(rr_wide)[grepl("^Lag 21", names(rr_wide))]

if (length(n7) != 1 || length(n14) != 1 || length(n21) != 1) {
  stop("Could not identify all three cumulative RR curves.")
}

rr_wide <- rr_wide %>%
  mutate(
    difference_14_vs_7 = abs(.data[[n14]] - .data[[n7]]),
    difference_21_vs_14 = abs(.data[[n21]] - .data[[n14]]),
    difference_21_vs_7 = abs(.data[[n21]] - .data[[n7]])
  )

curve_difference_summary <- data.frame(
  comparison = c(
    "Lag14 versus Lag7",
    "Lag21 versus Lag14",
    "Lag21 versus Lag7"
  ),
  maximum_absolute_difference = c(
    max(rr_wide$difference_14_vs_7, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(rr_wide$difference_21_vs_14, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(rr_wide$difference_21_vs_7, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  mean_absolute_difference = c(
    mean(rr_wide$difference_14_vs_7, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(rr_wide$difference_21_vs_14, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(rr_wide$difference_21_vs_7, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  curve_difference_summary,
  digits = 3,
  caption =
    "Differences between cumulative RR curves across alternative lag windows."
)

write.csv(
  curve_difference_summary,
  "outputs/Cumulative_RR_curve_difference_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MMT AND RR SUMMARY
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

lag_summary <- rr_all %>%
  group_by(lag) %>%
  summarise(
    MMT_C = utci[which.min(rr)],
    minimum_cumulative_RR = min(rr, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_cumulative_RR = max(rr, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  lag_summary,
  digits = 3,
  caption =
    "Cumulative exposure-response summary for Lag7_E3_L3, Lag14_E3_L3 and Lag21_E3_L3."
)

write.csv(
  lag_summary,
  "outputs/Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# EXPOSURE-LAG-RESPONSE SURFACES
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cumul = FALSE is intentional here.
# The surface must show RR separately at each exposure x lag combination.
# The cumulative analysis above uses cumul = TRUE.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_surface_data <- function(fit, cb, max_lag, lag_label, x_seq) {

  cp <- dlnm::crosspred(
    cb,
    model = fit,
    at = x_seq,
    cen = NA,
    cumul = FALSE
  )

  rr_mat <- as.matrix(cp$matRRfit)
  lag_values <- seq(0, max_lag)

  if (ncol(rr_mat) != length(lag_values)) {
    stop(
      lag_label,
      ": expected ", length(lag_values),
      " lag columns but found ", ncol(rr_mat), "."
    )
  }

  out <- expand.grid(
    utci = x_seq,
    lag_day = lag_values
  )

  out$rr <- as.vector(rr_mat)
  out$lag_window <- lag_label

  out
}

surface7 <- make_surface_data(
  fit7, cb7, 7, "Lag 7 days", x_seq
)

surface14 <- make_surface_data(
  fit14, cb14, 14, "Lag 14 days", x_seq
)

surface21 <- make_surface_data(
  fit21, cb21, 21, "Lag 21 days", x_seq
)

surface_all <- bind_rows(
  surface7, surface14, surface21
)

write.csv(
  surface_all,
  "outputs/Exposure_Lag_Response_Surface_Data_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3D PLOT FUNCTION
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

plot_3d_surface <- function(surface_data, title_text) {

  if (!requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop(
      "Package 'plotly' is required for the 3D exposure-lag-response ",
      "surfaces. Install it with install.packages('plotly')."
    )
  }

  x_values <- sort(unique(surface_data$utci))
  lag_values <- sort(unique(surface_data$lag_day))

  z_matrix <- matrix(
    surface_data$rr,
    nrow = length(x_values),
    ncol = length(lag_values),
    byrow = FALSE
  )

  plotly::plot_ly(
    x = x_values,
    y = lag_values,
    z = z_matrix
  ) %>%
    plotly::add_surface() %>%
    plotly::layout(
      title = title_text,
      scene = list(
        xaxis = list(title = "UTCI (°C)"),
        yaxis = list(title = "Lag (days)"),
        zaxis = list(title = "Relative risk")
      )
    )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THREE SEPARATE 3D SURFACES
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

p3d_lag7 <- plot_3d_surface(
  surface7,

)

p3d_lag14 <- plot_3d_surface(

)

p3d_lag7

  group_by(lag_day) %>%

write.csv(
  incremental_summary,

)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LAG DECISION TABLE
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

lag_decision_table <- data.frame(

    "Lag7_E3_L3",

message("")
```

## Manual primary-lag lock

After reviewing all outputs, return to the `PRIMARY_LAG` block near the
beginning of the analysis and uncomment **only one** of the following.

```{r manual_primary_lag_lock, eval=FALSE}
# PRIMARY_LAG <- 7
# PRIMARY_LAG <- 14
# PRIMARY_LAG <- 21
```

For example, if the empirical comparison demonstrates that Lag 14 is the
most appropriate primary lag:

```{r manual_primary_lag_example, eval=FALSE}
PRIMARY_LAG <- 14
```

Do not leave more than one of the three assignments uncommented.

## Propagate the manually selected lag to downstream analyses

Once the primary lag has been manually locked, use the selected value
throughout Objectives 1–4 rather than hard-coding a separate lag in each
section.

```{r propagate_primary_lag, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (is.null(PRIMARY_LAG)) {
  stop(
    "PRIMARY_LAG has not been manually locked. ",
    "Review the Lag7/Lag14/Lag21 cumulative RR and 3D results first, ",
    "then uncomment exactly one PRIMARY_LAG assignment."
  )
}

PRIMARY_LAG_LABEL <- paste0("Lag", PRIMARY_LAG)

PRIMARY_MODEL_ID <- paste0(
  "Lag", PRIMARY_LAG, "_E3_L3"
)

PRIMARY_LAG
PRIMARY_LAG_LABEL
PRIMARY_MODEL_ID
```

All downstream primary analyses should use:

```{r downstream_primary_lag_template, eval=FALSE}
max_lag <- PRIMARY_LAG
```


This ensures that once the empirical lag comparison has been reviewed, the
same manually selected lag is propagated consistently through the primary
exposure-response, temporal-shift, vulnerable-group, meta-analytic and
attributable-burden analyses.

# Objective 2: Characterize lag effects

Objective 2 retains all three maximum-lag structures (7, 14 and 21 days).
The manually selected `PRIMARY_LAG` is used only for the primary downstream
analysis; the alternative lag windows remain available as sensitivity and
lag-structure analyses.


# Objective 2: Characterize lag effects

Objective 2 retains the full 0–21-day lag information. Maximum lags 7, 14,
and 21 days are reported as distinct lag-window analyses rather than allowing
model selection to silently discard a biologically relevant lag structure.

```{r}

# ============================================================
# LOCKED PRIMARY CANDIDATE SPECIFICATION: E3_L3
# ============================================================
# E3_L3 is the fixed exposure/lag basis specification.
# Lag duration is NOT selected automatically.
# The three prespecified candidates are:
#   Lag 7  + E3_L3
#   Lag 14 + E3_L3
#   Lag 21 + E3_L3
#
# The analyst reviews the formal Lag 7/14/21 comparison and
# manually locks PRIMARY_LAG to 7, 14, or 21.
# ============================================================

PRIMARY_EXPOSURE_DF <- 3
PRIMARY_LAG_DF      <- 3
PRIMARY_SPEC_ID     <- "E3_L3"

required_models <- c("Lag7_E3_L3", "Lag14_E3_L3", "Lag21_E3_L3")

if (!all(required_models %in% candidate_specs$model_id)) {
  missing_models <- setdiff(required_models, candidate_specs$model_id)
  stop(
    "Required E3_L3 candidate model(s) are missing: ",
    paste(missing_models, collapse = ", "),
    "."
  )
}

spec_lag7 <- candidate_specs %>% dplyr::filter(model_id == "Lag7_E3_L3")
spec_lag14 <- candidate_specs %>% dplyr::filter(model_id == "Lag14_E3_L3")
spec_lag21 <- candidate_specs %>% dplyr::filter(model_id == "Lag21_E3_L3")

if (nrow(spec_lag7) != 1 || nrow(spec_lag14) != 1 || nrow(spec_lag21) != 1) {
  stop("Expected exactly one specification for each E3_L3 lag candidate.")
}

best_spec_lag7 <- list(
  model_id = "Lag7_E3_L3",
  max_lag = 7,
  exposure_df = spec_lag7$exposure_df[[1]],
  lag_df = spec_lag7$lag_df[[1]]
)

best_spec_lag14 <- list(
  model_id = "Lag14_E3_L3",
  max_lag = 14,
  exposure_df = spec_lag14$exposure_df[[1]],
  lag_df = spec_lag14$lag_df[[1]]
)

best_spec_lag21 <- list(
  model_id = "Lag21_E3_L3",
  max_lag = 21,
  exposure_df = spec_lag21$exposure_df[[1]],
  lag_df = spec_lag21$lag_df[[1]]
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# REFIT THE THREE E3_L3 CANDIDATES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fit_lag7_e3_l3 <- run_dlnm_spec(
  dat,
  max_lag = best_spec_lag7$max_lag,
  exposure_df = best_spec_lag7$exposure_df,
  lag_df = best_spec_lag7$lag_df
)

fit_lag14_e3_l3 <- run_dlnm_spec(
  dat,
  max_lag = best_spec_lag14$max_lag,
  exposure_df = best_spec_lag14$exposure_df,
  lag_df = best_spec_lag14$lag_df
)

fit_lag21_e3_l3 <- run_dlnm_spec(
  dat,
  max_lag = best_spec_lag21$max_lag,
  exposure_df = best_spec_lag21$exposure_df,
  lag_df = best_spec_lag21$lag_df
)

if (is.null(fit_lag7_e3_l3)) stop("Lag7_E3_L3 could not be refitted.")
if (is.null(fit_lag14_e3_l3)) stop("Lag14_E3_L3 could not be refitted.")
if (is.null(fit_lag21_e3_l3)) stop("Lag21_E3_L3 could not be refitted.")

# Preserve fit-specific knots and centering.
best_spec_lag7$var_knots <- fit_lag7_e3_l3$var_knots
best_spec_lag7$lag_knots <- fit_lag7_e3_l3$lag_basis$knots
best_spec_lag7$MMT <- fit_lag7_e3_l3$MMT
best_spec_lag7$cen <- fit_lag7_e3_l3$MMT

best_spec_lag14$var_knots <- fit_lag14_e3_l3$var_knots
best_spec_lag14$lag_knots <- fit_lag14_e3_l3$lag_basis$knots
best_spec_lag14$MMT <- fit_lag14_e3_l3$MMT
best_spec_lag14$cen <- fit_lag14_e3_l3$MMT

best_spec_lag21$var_knots <- fit_lag21_e3_l3$var_knots
best_spec_lag21$lag_knots <- fit_lag21_e3_l3$lag_basis$knots
best_spec_lag21$MMT <- fit_lag21_e3_l3$MMT
best_spec_lag21$cen <- fit_lag21_e3_l3$MMT

# Save all candidates for auditability.
saveRDS(best_spec_lag7, "Results/Objects/spec_Lag7_E3_L3.rds")
saveRDS(best_spec_lag14, "Results/Objects/spec_Lag14_E3_L3.rds")
saveRDS(best_spec_lag21, "Results/Objects/spec_Lag21_E3_L3.rds")

saveRDS(fit_lag7_e3_l3, "Results/Objects/model_Lag7_E3_L3.rds")
saveRDS(fit_lag14_e3_l3, "Results/Objects/model_Lag14_E3_L3.rds")
saveRDS(fit_lag21_e3_l3, "Results/Objects/model_Lag21_E3_L3.rds")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# MANUAL PRIMARY-LAG LOCK
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Review the Lag 7 / Lag 14 / Lag 21 E3_L3 comparison FIRST.
# Then uncomment EXACTLY ONE of the following:
#
# PRIMARY_LAG <- 7
# PRIMARY_LAG <- 14
# PRIMARY_LAG <- 21

PRIMARY_LAG <- NULL

if (!is.null(PRIMARY_LAG) && !PRIMARY_LAG %in% c(7, 14, 21)) {
  stop("PRIMARY_LAG must be NULL, 7, 14, or 21.")
}

```

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PROPAGATE THE MANUALLY LOCKED PRIMARY MODEL
# ------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}

if (!is.null(PRIMARY_LAG)) {

  if (PRIMARY_LAG == 7) {
    best_spec <- best_spec_lag7
    best_fit <- fit_lag7_e3_l3
  } else if (PRIMARY_LAG == 14) {
    best_spec <- best_spec_lag14
    best_fit <- fit_lag14_e3_l3
  } else {
    best_spec <- best_spec_lag21
    best_fit <- fit_lag21_e3_l3
  }

  MMT <- best_fit$MMT
  cb <- best_fit$cb
  fit <- best_fit$fit
  final_pred <- best_fit$pred
  max_lag <- PRIMARY_LAG

  PRIMARY_LAG_LABEL <- paste0("Lag", PRIMARY_LAG)
  PRIMARY_MODEL_ID <- paste0("Lag", PRIMARY_LAG, "_E3_L3")

  saveRDS(best_spec, "Results/Objects/best_specification.rds")
  saveRDS(best_fit, "Results/Objects/best_model.rds")

  write.csv(
    as.data.frame(best_fit$metrics),
    "Results/Crossbasis/Locked_Model_Diagnostics.csv",
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  message("PRIMARY MODEL LOCKED: ", PRIMARY_MODEL_ID)

} else {

  message(
    "PRIMARY_LAG is NULL. The three E3_L3 candidates remain available ",
    "for manual Lag 7 / Lag 14 / Lag 21 selection. ",
    "No primary model has been locked."
  )
}
```
